title: Local section comparison of a short complex from first-cohomology vanishing
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme, $V\subseteq Y$ an open, and $S=(M_1\xrightarrow f M_2\xrightarrow g M_3)$ a short complex of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules, so $gf=0$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $U$ forget the sheaf condition, $L$ be exact sheafification, and $\epsilon:LU\to\mathrm{id}$ their adjunction counit. Homology means $\ker g/\operatorname{im}f$. Suppose $H^1(V,(\ker f)|_V)=0$ and $H^1(V,(\operatorname{im} f)|_V)=0$, with module right-derived global sections [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology]. Form $c:L\mathcal H(US)\to\mathcal H(S)$ by the inverse exact-sheafification homology comparison $L\mathcal H(US)\to\mathcal H(LUS)$ followed by $\mathcal H(\epsilon_S)$. Then evaluation over $V$ of the adjoint $\mathcal H(US)\to U\mathcal H(S)$ of $c$ is an isomorphism of additive groups. No acyclicity of the three terms or the homology object, and no surrounding complex, is assumed.

proof.text: Put $Z=\ker g$, $B=\operatorname{im}f$, and $N=\ker f$. Restriction to $V$ is exact. The initial long exact sequence for $0\to N\to M_1\to B\to0$ and $H^1(V,N)=0$ give surjectivity of $\Gamma(V,M_1)\to\Gamma(V,B)$. The sequence for $0\to B\to Z\to\mathcal H(S)\to0$ and $H^1(V,B)=0$ gives surjectivity of $\Gamma(V,Z)\to\Gamma(V,\mathcal H(S))$ with kernel $\Gamma(V,B)$. Identify derived degree zero with ordinary sections using Functor.rightDerivedZeroIsoSelf.

Left exactness of sections identifies $\Gamma(V,Z)$ with the kernel of $\Gamma(V,g)$. The two surjections identify $\Gamma(V,\mathcal H(S))$ with the cokernel of the incoming map to that kernel. Exact evaluation of presheaves identifies the source with the homology of the section short complex, giving an isomorphism.

Identify this isomorphism with the displayed adjunction-defined map. The exact-sheafification homology comparison takes a sheafified cycle class to the class of that cycle. The counit returns its representative to $S$, and the adjunction unit sheafifies the original presheaf class. Thus the composite sends a section cycle to its class in $\mathcal H(S)$. Precompose both maps with the epimorphic homology projection from section cycles; their equality there is this calculation, so they are equal. The zero incoming map and empty open are covered by the same kernel and cokernel universal properties.

theorem shortComplex_sectionComparison_isIso
    {Y : Scheme.{u}} (S : ShortComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} Y.ringCatSheaf))
    (V : Y.Opens)
    (hkernel : IsZero ((RingedSpace.moduleCohomology V.toScheme.toRingedSpace 1).obj
      ((restrictFunctor V.ι).obj (kernel S.f))))
    (himage : IsZero ((RingedSpace.moduleCohomology V.toScheme.toRingedSpace 1).obj
      ((restrictFunctor V.ι).obj (image S.f)))) :
    IsIso (((PresheafOfModules.toPresheaf.{u} Y.ringCatSheaf.obj).map
      ((PresheafOfModules.sheafificationAdjunction.{u} (𝟙 Y.ringCatSheaf.obj)).homEquiv
        (S.map (SheafOfModules.forget.{u} Y.ringCatSheaf)).homology S.homology
        (((S.map (SheafOfModules.forget.{u} Y.ringCatSheaf)).mapHomologyIso
          (PresheafOfModules.sheafification.{u} (𝟙 Y.ringCatSheaf.obj))).inv ≫
          ShortComplex.homologyMap (S.mapNatTrans
            (PresheafOfModules.sheafificationAdjunction.{u}
              (𝟙 Y.ringCatSheaf.obj)).counit)))).app (op V))
